overall: Atlanta is tracking a hot afternoon on June 10, with the running max reaching 87.8°F by 15:35 ET and a still-positive velocity of +1.8°F/hr suggesting peak heating has not yet fully arrived. The temperature has risen steadily all day — nearly 13°F from the morning — and the high dewpoint of 71.6°F indicates a moist, humid airmass that is sustaining the heat load. The day is running hotter than at least two of the four models forecast, which is a meaningful signal.
forecast_obs_notes: There is notable model spread today: GFS and HRRR are tightly clustered at 89.4°F, while ECMWF (85.6°F) and NBM (86.8°F) are both already breached by observed temperatures as of mid-afternoon, undermining their credibility for today's high. The GFS/HRRR consensus is now better aligned with observed reality and deserves higher weighting going forward.
max_temp_prediction: With a running max of 87.8°F, an active warming velocity of +1.8°F/hr, and peak heating typically occurring between 3–5 PM ET in Atlanta in June, there is meaningful upside remaining. The GFS/HRRR 89.4°F target is well-supported, and a final high in the 88.5–89.5°F range is most likely; confidence is moderate-to-high given two models already beaten and positive velocity still in play, though the 35-minute plateau in the running max introduces some uncertainty about whether the peak may be imminent.
